channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average tags a record, then hides behind its dullest stocks
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average spent Tuesday arriving late to a party the rest of the market had already begun to leave.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar weakens as Middle East tensions lift US Dollar ahead RBNZ hike
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5685 at the time of writing on Tuesday, down 0.26% on the day.

item.title: Germany: Factory recovery prospects – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Ralph Solveen notes that German industrial output rose 0.9% in May versus April, leaving April–May production slightly above the first-quarter average.

item.title: WTI climbs over 2% as Strait of Hormuz attacks revive supply concerns
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude Oil edges higher on Tuesday as fresh attacks near the Strait of Hormuz threaten the recovery in shipping seen in recent weeks following the interim US-Iran peace deal. At the time of writing, WTI is trading around $70.44, up about 2.65% on the day.

item.title: British Pound slips as Hormuz attacks revive USD demand
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) retreats against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday as tensions in the Middle East rise, following reports of attacks on two ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The GBP/USD pair trades at 1.3373, down 0.11%.

item.title: Canada: Trade surplus widens as investment rises – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economists Abbey Xu and Nathan Janzen note that Canada’s merchandise trade surplus increased to $4.2 billion in May from $3.4 billion in April, as exports grew and imports slipped.

item.title: Euro: Upside bias against US Dollar as ECB repriced – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report the Euro (EUR) is slightly softer versus the US Dollar (USD) but supported by a sharp recovery in yield spreads and stronger German industrial production.

item.title: Australian Dollar falls amid cautious Fedspeak
item.description: AUD/USD declines toward 0.6940 as the Australian Dollar (AUD) loses momentum, while the US Dollar (USD) remains supported by cautious remarks from the Federal Reserve (Fed) and lingering uncertainty over inflation.

item.title: Silver falls below $61 as markets await Fed minutes
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) extends its decline for a second consecutive day on Tuesday, trading around $60.70 at the time of writing, down 2.21% on the day.

item.title: NY Fed inflation expectations jump despite lower gas prices
item.description: The New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations shows that Americans are growing worried about the high cost of living, as one-year inflation expectations rose from 3.5% in May to 3.7% in June, the highest level since September 2023.

item.title: Swiss Franc eases as hawkish Fed outlook supports US Dollar
item.description: USD/CHF holds modest gains on Tuesday as traders balance softer US labor market data against hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations, keeping the US Dollar (USD) range-bound. At the time of writing, the pair is trading around 0.8066, remaining on the front foot for a second consecutive day.

item.title: National Bank of Poland: Wait-and-see stance holds – ING
item.description: ING economists Rafal Benecki and Adam Antoniak expect the National Bank of Poland (NBP) to keep interest rates unchanged at 3.75% on 9 July and through year-end, with hikes ruled out and cuts seen as unlikely in the near term.

item.title: Oil: Gulf supply recovery challenges oversupply narrative – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch highlights a rapid recovery in Gulf oil production and exports following the US–Iran agreement, with Brent moving into contango and Saudi Arabia slashing its OSP for Asian buyers.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Near historic lows against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight the Japanese Yen (JPY) as the best-performing G10 currency on the day, though gains versus the US Dollar (USD) are marginal.

item.title: Gold stalls recovery as traders eye FOMC meeting minutes
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) stalls its recovery and trades on the back foot for a second consecutive day on Tuesday as a steady US Dollar (USD) and doubts over the Federal Reserve's (Fed) interest rate path keep the upside in check.

item.title: Euro: ECB cautious as euro area outlook stays fragile – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu cites European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member Fabio Panetta, who describes a fragile Euro area outlook with upside inflation risks and downside growth risks.

item.title: Canadian Dollar holds steady despite solid trade data, higher Oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.4205 on Tuesday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day, as investors balance encouraging Canadian economic data against a US Dollar (USD) that remains supported by monetary policy expectations and ongoing geopolitical tensions.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Weak against US Dollar with limited upside – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada ’s (NBC) Stéfane Marion and Kyle Dahms highlight the Japanese Yen (JPY) trading near multi-decade lows around 161 per USD, even as long-end yield differentials move in Japan’s favour.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Bearish bias persists below 0.8600
item.description: EUR/GBP trades with a positive bias on Tuesday as sellers take a breather following the recent selloff that pushed the cross to a more than one-year low. At the time of writing, EUR/GBP is trading around 0.8550 after rebounding from an intraday low of 0.8533, its lowest level since June 2025.

item.title: British Pound: Capped by layered resistance against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the British Pound (GBP) is slightly softer against the US Dollar (USD) after encountering resistance near 1.3400, with limited fresh data and Bank of England (BoE) news.

item.title: Fed’s Williams: “Monetary policy is in a good place”
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of New York President John Williams said on Tuesday that the United States (US) economy continues to show steady, trend-like growth, while the labor market remains stable.

item.title: Aluminium: Short supply supports prices despite Gulf outages – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Barbara Lambrecht says Aluminium’s recent correction has likely run its course, with prices rebounding as Chinese and LME inventories fall sharply and Gulf smelter outages persist.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Japan denies rate-pressure claims as data mixed – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu notes Japan’s Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi rejected reports that the government is trying to push interest rates lower or pressure the Bank of Japan (BoJ).

item.title: Oil: Deficits support higher prices – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Ryan McKay argues that Crude Oil is far from oversupplied, with high-frequency global and Chinese balances still pointing to tightness.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Consolidation with stretched USD positioning – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is effectively flat versus the US Dollar (USD) and trading close to their fair value estimate around 1.4158. They expect the recent deterioration in spreads to stabilize, easing downside pressure on the CAD.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Policy seen on hold through 2026 – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economist Claire Fan notes that the Q2 2026 Bank of Canada Business Outlook Survey showed resilient sales and investment expectations despite earlier Oil price shocks.

item.title: Polish Zloty: Dovish NBP tone risks downside – ING
item.description: ING economists Rafal Benecki and Adam Antoniak argue that reduced prospects of further tightening by the European Central Bank (ECB) and Federal Reserve (Fed) should ease external pressure on the Zloty.

item.title: Euro holds steady as traders assess Fed and ECB interest rate paths
item.description: EUR/USD trades in a narrow range on Tuesday as traders await greater clarity on the Federal Reserve's (Fed) and European Central Bank's (ECB) interest rate paths. At the time of writing, EUR/USD is trading around 1.1436, little changed on the day.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Fiscal unease and BoJ path – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes the Japanese Yen (JPY) has firmed slightly, pulling USD/JPY back from 162.18 to 161.68, as comments from Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuichi attempt to calm fiscal worries.

item.title: Gold: Price dip seen limited as PBoC buying continues – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch notes Gold fell to USD 4,120 per ounce after fresh Iranian attacks lifted TTF gas and Oil prices, but Fed rate expectations remain unchanged.
